data.one_liner: Connect to a Pusher server using WebSockets across all platforms.
data.what_it_does: Allows Flutter applications to connect to Pusher-compatible WebSocket servers. It supports subscribing to public, private, private encrypted, and presence channels, binding event listeners, and automatic reconnection.
use_when: You need real-time messaging or broadcasting using Pusher or compatible servers like Laravel Reverb.
You require cross-platform support for public, private, or presence channels.
avoid_when: You are using standard REST APIs without real-time socket requirements.
You require a backend client rather than a Flutter frontend client.
strengths: Supports all platforms including Android, iOS, Web, macOS, Windows, and Linux.
Handles automatic reconnection and activity checks out-of-the-box.
Supports encrypted and presence channels with custom authentication headers.
weaknesses: Limited documentation outside of basic usage and options table.

alternatives.name: web_socket_channel
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want a standard, low-level WebSocket wrapper without Pusher-specific protocol overhead.

alternatives.name: http
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you only need standard REST communication rather than real-time channels.
